gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Nomad's Modern Leather Folio for iPhone 17 is $74 today on nomadgoods.com (25% Black Friday markdown from $99). Of the priced cases with built-in card storage, it is the only one whose maker claims MagSafe and Qi2 charging, so it now costs about $11 more than the $62.99 2-in-1 leather wallet ChatGPT ranked first (not the $25 more ChatGPT's '~$99' implies). Smartish's two Wallet Slayers charge by cable only. ZEERA's store lists the $19.99 MagWeave Pro that ChatGPT showed for the iPhone 17 under the iPhone 17 Pro Max and 18 Pro Max.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best iPhone 17 cases (cited). The part of the page I could read named no card or wallet case and gave no prices; WebFetch returned a truncated page. Also compared against Apple's Accessory Design Guidelines (cited), which only advise against rear card pockets on wireless-charging cases and price nothing. ChatGPT's own answers priced Nomad at 'around $99' and Decoded at 'around $60', and labelled ZEERA as an iPhone 17 option. No result showed today's sale price, the cable-only status of the Smartish cases, or ZEERA's model listing. Wired, Digital Camera World and rottenwifi were not opened, so they were not checked.
decides: This supports keeping Nomad Modern Leather Folio as the pick for 'cards built in and MagSafe charging'. At $74 the cost argument for detachable 2-in-1 wallets (TORRO-style about $63, Decoded about $60) mostly goes away, and those need the wallet removed before charging. For a budget build, Smartish Gripmunk with MagSafe ($19.99) plus a separate MagSafe wallet stays the cheapest way to get working MagSafe charging, though the wallet has to come off. Wallet Slayer Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 lose for this question because they are cable-charge only. ZEERA MagWeave Pro should be checked before it is recommended for a base iPhone 17.
